subject: Sourcing evaluation: credit card blockers and PO timeline
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@solara.io>; Procurement Ops <procurement@solara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Sourcing evaluation: credit card blockers and PO timeline

Hi Samir / procurement team —

Great to meet yesterday. Quick recap from our call and concrete next steps so we can validate the commercial path for the pilot.

Recap (short):
- Pilot scope: 3 dedicated GPU slots, 6 months, internal-only VPC.
- Primary blocking question from your AP team: can Solara pay via corporate card (preferred) or will a PO + standard 30-day net be required for onboarding?
- Marketplace option discussed: you mentioned your vendor management prefers marketplace procurement where available to speed security reviews.

What we need to close procurement readiness:
1) Confirmation from AP whether corporate card is allowed for initial pilot purchases under $50k (Samir noted $10k/month expected spend).
2) If PO required: which internal form (PO template) do we need and typical lead time to issue?
3) Marketplace: are you willing to pursue marketplace procurement if it reduces paperwork? Who owns the marketplace procurement (vendor vs IT)?

Action items (my side):
- Attached: draft quote (redwood-quote-v1.pdf) and a short AP checklist (procurement-checklist.xlsx) for you to share with Aisha / AP.
- If PO path: we can provide a simplified SOW + commercial T&Cs to speed your buyer and legal review.

Proposed timeline:
- Today: Samir / Aisha confirm card vs PO preference and whether marketplace is an option.
- By Fri (6/25): if PO required, receive blank PO template and expected issue date; if card allowed, we share payment link and onboarding guide.

Thanks — happy to jump on a 15-min call later today if it helps.

Best,
Alex
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex.martinez@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: redwood-quote-v1.pdf (PDF, 3p), procurement-checklist.xlsx (Excel, 1 sheet)

From: Samir Shah <samir.shah@solara.io>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Ops <procurement@solara.io>, Aisha R. (Finance) <aisha@solara.io>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sourcing evaluation: credit card blockers and PO timeline

Alex —

Thanks for the clear recap and the attachments. Aisha and I discussed this this morning. Short answers:

- Card: EV team has a $25k monthly spend ceiling on corpcards for SaaS trials. Anything above needs a PO.
- PO: our standard PO process takes 7-10 business days once we have the vendor setup completed in Coupa. Vendor setup requires W-9 + bank remit info + 2 security attestations.
- Marketplace: we can do marketplace procurement if the vendor is listed. Marketplace orders can be turned around in 2-3 business days typically.

Open questions for Redwood:
1) Do you appear on any cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure) or partner marketplaces where Solara already buys? If so, how soon could you be listed?
2) For the PO path, we need a Remit/Banking contact and W-9 — do you have a single point we can share with AP?

I can escalate a quick vendor-setup exception if we need to get a PO out faster, but I need the items above.

- Samir
Director, Strategic Sourcing | Solara Energy

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Shah <samir.shah@solara.io>, Procurement Ops <procurement@solara.io>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 13:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Sourcing evaluation: credit card blockers and PO timeline

Samir —

Great, thanks for the clarity. Answers below so you can pass to Aisha / AP.

1) Marketplaces: Redwood is currently available on AWS Marketplace (Redwood Inference, seller account: redwood-inference). Listing process is underway for GCP Marketplace — timeline ~3-4 weeks if you elect to go that route. If you can consume the pilot via AWS Marketplace we can use that path for the fastest procurement and reduced internal paperwork.

2) Remit/W-9: W-9 and remit details attached — please use payments@redwood.com as the remit contact and ACH details in the W-9 doc. (We included both the W-9 and a minimal vendor setup packet in the Drive link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/solara-procurement-evidence)

3) If you want to keep spend under the corpcard ceiling for month one, we can split the pilot into a two-invoice approach: initial month via card up to $25k, remainder invoiced on PO once vendor setup completes. That typically preserves momentum.

Next steps I recommend:
- Aisha: confirm whether Solara is OK with the split-invoice approach. If yes, we can start onboarding tomorrow and Redwood will invoice month 1 to card.
- Samir: share marketplace ownership contact if marketplace is preferred — we will pull listing details and provide SKU/pricing.

If helpful, I can loop our payments ops lead (Ben Carter) for vendor setup questions — Ben, can you confirm you can provide the W-9 + bank remit confirmation to Solara's AP?

Thanks,
Alex

> On Mon, Jun 21, 2026 at 11:03 AM Samir Shah <samir.shah@solara.io> wrote:
> "Card: EV team has a $25k monthly spend ceiling on corpcards for SaaS trials. Anything above needs a PO."

From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 21 Jun 2026 16:45:00 -0700
Subject: INTERNAL: quick sync — Solara AP blockers and next steps

Marissa / Ben —

Quick internal note after Samir's replies:
- Solara can do card up to $25k / month; expected pilot spend ~ $10k/mo, so corpcard path is viable for month 1.
- PO process 7-10 bd + vendor setup through Coupa (W-9 + bank + security attestations) — Ben, we should send the vendor setup packet today so they can run Coupa intake.
- Marketplace (AWS) is the fastest path if they choose it; ask Samir if his cloud procurement team will own that.

Recommended play: offer the split invoice (card first month, PO for later months) and prepare a short vendor setup packet (W-9, remit, SOC2 pointer, minimal attestation). I've attached the quote and checklist in the outbound thread.

I'll wait for Aisha's confirmation. If she agrees, we push onboarding for Tue.

Alex
Account Executive
